title: Alonso Sánchez (Venice) to Charles V, May–August 1523 — RAH Salazar 9/28, DECODE R9670–R9770

steps.what: Found the ten records in the DECODE group harvest (Salazar 9/28, author Alonso Sánchez), pulled record pages and metadata; all flagged Inline Cleartext: Yes. Fetched 32 images.

Viewed the images: no interlinear or facing decipherment; 'Inline Cleartext' means clear passages. Same hand and cipher as the 1522 despatches; letters addressed to the Emperor, not an unknown recipient.

Fetched Bergenroth CSP Spain vol. 2 (1523) from British History Online; nos. 549, 552, 554, 558 are these despatches (Salazar A-28, matching folios), each 'Autograph in cipher. Contemporary deciphering.'
Mapped each record to a CSP entry by date line, content and folio; R9670/R9674/R9690/R9770 are duplicates; R9767, R9769, R9770 (16 Aug 1523) are not calendared.
Applied the 1522 key (targets/sanchez1522/key_codes.tsv) to code groups on R9670, R9671, R9672, R9677, R9767: they read coherently; key unchanged into 1523.

Read R9767 (16 Aug 1523): clear text in full; cipher passages at code-group level, spelled runs partly. Gist: French-leaning party in Venice, the treaty's money clause, the Infante not bound to the defensive league.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked Bergenroth's CSP abstracts (R9670-R9690) and read_r9767.md; no ciphertext transcriptions; R9769/R9770 not transcribed

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): read_r9767.md and csp/bergenroth_abstracts.txt read. The seven calendared letters read through Bergenroth's coherent English abstracts of the contemporary decipherings (reviewed B, language en); R9767's cipher passages are [code] strings with … between them (gist only) and R9769/R9770 have no file. R9767, R9769 and R9770 relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved kept.

Re-read b34: fetched the record pages of the neighbouring DECODE records R9764-R9766, R9768, R9771, R9772 and the four images of R9768 (ff. 565-568, Alonso Sánchez, status Decrypted, never fetched before). R9768 is the second copy of R9767 (f. 565r cipher, f. 566r clear close) and f. 567r is the contemporary decipherment of R9767's two cipher passages. Opened all images of R9769 and R9770: R9769 f. 570v carries a nine-line cipher paragraph after the date (not noticed in Sept), and R9770 f. 574r is its contemporary decipherment.
Transcribed the two contemporary decipherments (R9767_decifrado_f567r.txt, R9770_decifrado_f574r.txt) and the whole clear text of the joint letter R9769 from full-resolution crops.

Aligned the cipher of R9767 f. 563r and R9769 f. 570v group by group with the decipherments (R9767_cipher_align.md, R9769_reread_log.md). All codes but one are in the 1522 key; the figures agree with the decipherments except two places in R9767 ('porque dan los' for 'por dar a los'; 'una paz' for 'paz'), where the readings follow the figures. Corrected the earlier partial decode: xug was spelled m-a-l, yol is yoh = causa, the run after suf is expremido.

New code value pem = -mos, adopted: it holds at all three occurrences (diximos in R9767; prometiessemos, procuraremos in R9769), each under a contemporary decipherment, and its alphabetical slot (between pol 'mi' and ne 'muy') fits. Proposed for sanchez1522/key_codes.tsv, not written there.

Wrote R9767_reading.md and R9769_reading.md (with English) and scored the reading bodies: R9767 0.684 (13/19) plain, 1.000 explicit holes only; R9769 0.575 (50/87) plain, failures only 1523 spellings, 1.000 explicit holes only. R9767 and R9769 marked read (grade A), R9770 read through R9769 (grade B).

outcome.method_basis: The code groups were read with Sánchez's own 1522 key (Tomokiyo, cryptiana AlonsoSanchez.htm 2025, extended in sanchez1522), unchanged into 1523; the May-June despatches were already calendared by Bergenroth (CSP Spain 2, nos. 549-558) from the contemporary decipherings.
outcome.notes: The May–June despatches were deciphered at the time and calendared in English by Bergenroth in 1866; the key was published by Tomokiyo in 2025. Added here: the records identified against the Calendar, the recipient corrected (Charles V), the 1522 key shown to hold in 1523, and (23 Oct 2026) the two uncalendared August letters read in full from contemporary decipherments found on neighbouring leaves (f. 567r on DECODE R9768 for R9767; f. 574r on R9770 for the joint letter R9769/R9770), each checked group by group against the cipher. New code value pem = -mos.

texts.label: R9670, 8 May 1523
texts.summary: Alonso Sánchez in Venice to Charles V. Doge Grimani's death and Cornaro's illness delay the negotiations with Venice; duplicate of the letter calendared as no. 549.
texts.note: Decryption: only Bergenroth's English abstract (CSP Spain 2, 1866, no. 549), made from the contemporary deciphering filed separately in the volume and not imaged; no transcription of the ciphertext.

reading_review.note: Bergenroth's English calendar abstract (CSP Spain 2, 1866) of the contemporary deciphering: coherent English sentences, a summary of the letter rather than its text, made from the decipherment of the time; kept as the reading of record (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R9767, 16 Aug 1523
texts.summary: Sánchez's own despatch of 16 August 1523, not calendared: the new Doge (Gritti) 'no es mal frances' but can do little harm; the capitulation expresses no cause for the Venetian money, which the ambassadors always said was paid for the perpetual peace, not for any right of the Empire or the House of Austria; the Infante not bound to the defensive league; navigation rights for Austria not obtained.

reading_review.note: R9767_reading.md follows the contemporary decipherment of both cipher passages, a court-hand clear copy on f. 567r found on DECODE R9768 (ff. 565-568, the second copy of the letter, never fetched before); aligned group by group with the cipher of f. 563r (R9767_cipher_align.md): agrees except 'porque dan los' (decipherment 'por dar a los') and 'una paz' (decipherment 'paz'), where the reading follows the figures. New code pem = -mos (3 occurrences under contemporary decipherments). Reading body 0.684 (13/19) plain, 1.000 (19/19) explicit holes only; one query ([?diversas], decipherment torn).

texts.label: R9769, 16 Aug 1523
texts.summary: Joint letter of Caracciolo and Sánchez, 16 August 1523: the peace and league with Venice, departures of the English and Austrian ambassadors, prisoners freed, the publication of the league, the Friuli restitution and the 38,000 ducats, Milan's bonds and the 500 men-at-arms, Mantua, Ferrara and Urbino and the captaincy; after the date, Sessa made a Venetian gentleman and a cipher paragraph on the instrument of mutual restitution (no obligation beyond 'procuraremos'), and Milan news.

reading_review.note: R9769_reading.md: the whole letter transcribed from R9769 (clear); its one cipher paragraph (f. 570v, not noticed in Sept) follows the contemporary decipherment on f. 574r (R9770 image P1), aligned group by group with the figures, which agree throughout. Reading body 0.575 (50/87) plain (1523 spellings only), 1.000 (87/87) explicit holes only. Open: one numeral before 'ducados de oro', [?possessiones], [?xxix].

texts.label: R9770, 16 Aug 1523
texts.summary: Duplicate of R9769 (joint letter of 16 August 1523), with a short cipher at the head of the last page and a clear note on the "mutua restitucion" instrument.

reading_review.note: R9770 is the copy ('es treslado de otra') of R9769 and carries the contemporary decipherment of the cipher paragraph on f. 574r; read through R9769_reading.md. Its cipher (f. 573r foot, f. 573v head) compared with R9769's at the legible groups (same); its clear text not collated word by word.
